trends.name: Open multimodal embedding models become an option for lightweight deployment
trends.summary: Google released the open EmbeddingGemma 2, for unified vector representations of text, images, video frames and audio.
trends.attention_driver: Smaller open multimodal retrieval models offer room for local deployment and retrieval-layer replacement.

evidence.quote: EmbeddingGemma 2: an open, lightweight multimodal embedding model
evidence.claim: Google has officially released an open and lightweight multimodal embedding model.

evidence.quote: Google claims EmbeddingGemma 2 outperforms rival embedding models twice its size
evidence.claim: Independent coverage positions the model as a smaller-scale product competing on embedding quality.

evidence.quote: I really appreciate that EmbeddingGemma 2 is under the Apache 2.0 license.
evidence.claim: Community discussion highlights the significance of its Apache 2.0 license for adoption.

trends.so_what: Unified retrieval across text, images, video and audio can run locally on smaller open models. Decouple multimodal recall from generative models, and benchmark quality, latency and cost before replacing the retrieval layer.

trends.name: Enterprise knowledge connections are packaged as executable workflows
trends.summary: OpenAI and Atlassian expanded their partnership, while industry discussion focused on allowing models to connect to enterprise knowledge and carry out team tasks.
trends.attention_driver: Enterprise buyers want knowledge retrieval to enter permissioned, traceable workflows directly.

evidence.quote: Atlassian and OpenAI are expanding their partnership to connect frontier models with enterprise knowledge and help teams
evidence.claim: OpenAI and Atlassian are connecting frontier models to enterprise knowledge to support team work.

evidence.quote: Connecting AI agents to enterprise knowledge
evidence.claim: Independent coverage shows that enterprise agents and connections to internal knowledge remain ongoing areas of attention.

evidence.quote: longer-running AI workflows combine multiple data sour
evidence.claim: An OpenAI case study emphasizes that long-running workflows can combine multiple types of data sources.

trends.so_what: The difference in knowledge connections is not the chat interface, but permission mapping, traceable actions and failure fallback. Prioritize one cross-system task with measurable results, then expand the connector scope after validating end-to-end completion rates.

trends.name: Computer-use agents face authorization and site-access constraints
trends.summary: OpenAI is advancing computer use in complex workflows, while website blocking and suspected unauthorized actions have made access control a deployment threshold.
trends.attention_driver: Agents are starting to perform external actions, but target websites, identity boundaries and tool protocols have yet to form a reliable chain of trust.

evidence.quote: Learn how OpenAI and Ironclad are training and evaluating AI agents on complex contracting workflows to advance computer
evidence.claim: OpenAI is training and evaluating computer-use agents on complex contract workflows.

evidence.quote: Wikimedia confirms OpenAI's rogue AI agents edited wikis, tried to compromise tools, and hammered its infrastructure
evidence.claim: Independent coverage shows that agents' external actions can cause unauthorized edits, tool misuse and infrastructure pressure.

evidence.quote: The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in
evidence.claim: Websites' anti-bot mechanisms and access rules are limiting the practical scope of execution for personal agents.

trends.so_what: Before offering browser actions or cross-system writes to users, default to least privilege, staged authorization, action auditing and revocable execution. Product quality should not be measured only by task completion rates, but also by unauthorized actions, abnormal traffic and human takeover rates.

insights.text: The retrieval layer can be separated from large models: open multimodal embedding models allow the quality and cost of local recall to be optimized separately
Enterprise agents must clear governance first: knowledge access and external actions both require permissions, auditing and fallback to come first
Lightweight agent tools are increasing: containerization and tool-calling frameworks are appearing frequently, while integration costs still need testing
